flc_001.why: Commons description 'Florencecourt Yew seen from (approx) NW', May 2010; whole broad shaggy yew with short red trunk fills a landscape frame; dense dark needles, yew; light WEAK (overcast sky) but colour and daylight.

dkh_001.why: Bregagh Road tunnel, October 2021 (recent, after the 2016 losses), geotag on the road; smooth pale grey sinuous beech trunks arching over the road, no people; centre band holds the tunnel; light OK.

rlg_001.why: Title names Reelig Glen's tallest Douglas firs, October 2022; two huge deeply furrowed Douglas fir trunks centred on the path beside the burn, a small group with backs turned for scale; crowns out of frame as for any 60 m fir; light OK.

inv_001.why: Description names the boulder at the foot of this oak as the Lord President Seat, bridge parapets behind match the setting; whole twisting oak, trunk and crown readable; bare (March 2010), daylight and colour; light OK.

gaf_001.why: Lone craggy wych elm on a stony slope in Gleann na Ciche, geotag about 25 m from our pin, June 2022 (before the 2024 planting); in leaf, crown and burred trunk fill the frame; light OK.

bmr_001.why: Benmore redwood avenue, geotag on the avenue, October 2012; both rows of red fibrous buttressed sequoia trunks framing the lawn, no people; centre band holds both rows; light OK.

cwl_001.why: Looked 2026-11-04: Commons file titled Giant Redwoods in the Castlewellan Castle Arboretum (Geograph import), 10 m from the pin; the red, fibrous sequoia trunks fill the frame, daylight.

crm_001.why: Looked 2026-11-04: Commons file titled Ancient Yew trees, Crom (Geograph import), 70 m from the pin; the whole low, spreading dome of the Crom yews fills the frame on the lawn, a person for scale, overcast daylight (photo_light WEAK).

'A magnificent oak in Kilbroney Park' is an upright deciduous tree on a lawn, not a leaning holm oak.
